answer: The paper's ITL formula ITL = alpha/(1 - lambda*W/N) holds in BLIS with R² = 0.915 (AL) and 0.944 (AD) across rates 1-150 req/s, with MAE < 0.63 ms on a 12-20 ms baseline. The formula correctly predicts that AD has lower ITL than AL at all rates (improvement 0.1-8.7%) and higher TTFT (penalty 10-52%). It breaks down above ~70 req/s where BLIS's token budget (max_num_scheduled_tokens=2048) caps batch size, causing observed ITL to plateau (~20 ms) while the formula predicts hyperbolic divergence. The breakdown mechanism is the mismatch between the M/G/1 unbounded-batch assumption and the simulator's vLLM-faithful token budget scheduler. For this configuration (512 prompt / 128 output tokens), W_P/W_D ≈ 0.16, so disaggregation provides a modest ITL benefit at the cost of substantial TTFT overhead from the prefill pipeline (~15.7 ms at low load, including KV transfer of ~3.4 ms).
